subject: Inference fleet service classification and scaling plan
messages:
From: Anya Petrov <anya@stratusdata.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-10T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Stratus / Redwood: dispatching fleet requirements + questionnaire

Hi Priyom / Jonas,

Thanks again for taking the time to review our on-prem requirements last week. Attached is the short questionnaire we promised — it has current traffic shape, peak windows, and a list of models we intend to serve from the private pool. We need Redwood's recommended service classification and sizing guidance so our ops team can provision equivalent racks on our side.

High-level asks from Stratus:
- Logical service tiers (latency-first vs throughput-first) with recommended per-tier throughput targets (qps or tokens/s).
- Suggested warm-pool strategy and prefill windows for bursty traffic (we see 80% of spikes within 30 min).
- Network egress/ingress constraints for colocated inference (we have 25 Gbps leaf uplinks, 10 Gbps per rack available for egress).
- Guidance on graceful degradation (fallback model map + retry windows).

Can you send a short classification proposal and an initial scale plan? If possible we’d like something we can hand to our procurement/infra teams by EOW.

Attachments: stratus_capacity_questionnaire.pdf

Thanks,
Anya
Anya Petrov
Solutions Architect, StratusData Solutions
anya@stratusdata.com

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Petrov <anya@stratusdata.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-10T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stratus / Redwood: dispatching fleet requirements + questionnaire

Anya — thanks for the questionnaire, that helps. Drafting a concise classification and scale proposal below so your infra/procurement teams have concrete numbers to work with. I attached a CSV with the same table.

Proposal: Inference fleet service classes (logical)
- Service Class A (latency-sensitive): target p50 <= 60ms for short-chat workloads; sustainable tail p99 <= 450ms under committed throughput. Target throughput: 250 qps per 8xA100-equivalent rack (mixed-request profile).
- Service Class B (balanced): target p50 <= 120ms, p99 <= 800ms. Target throughput: 700 qps per 8xA100-equivalent rack (batch-friendly requests allowed).
- Service Class C (throughput-first / large-batch): no hard p50 target; p99 <= 2s acceptable. Target throughput: 2k qps per 8xA100-equivalent rack when fully batched and KV cache hit-rate >= 70%.

Operational knobs and recommendations
- Warm pools: keep a configurable prefill corresponding to 15-25% of committed capacity for Classes A/B. Prefill window: 20–45 minutes depending on model load; we recommend a 30-minute default for burst-prone tenants. See prefill_latency_matrix.xlsx for warmup timelines by model family.
- KV cache priming: prioritize priming for Class A models at start-of-window; use short lived replicas for Class B during initial ramp to avoid contention.
- Routing matrix: route requests by service-class tag at the edge with capacity-aware admission control. Class A gets priority tokens up to a soft cap; overflow routes to lower-cost fallback model variant.
- Autoscale policy outline: scale increments by 1 rack once sustained utilization > 75% for 90s; scale-down when < 55% for 10m. For Class A, allow a short burst buffer (10%) with faster scale-out (30s sustained) using warm pool headroom.
- Networking: target per-rack egress headroom of 10 Gbps for Class A in heavy-media scenarios; ensure leaf-to-spine latency < 150us and avoid oversubscription above 5:1 during peak windows.
- Graceful degradation: maintain a prioritized model fallback map (A -> A-quantized -> B-variant -> small-embedding-only path). Max retry 2 times with exponential backoff starting at 50ms.

Next steps:
1) I will share the attached inference_service_classes.csv with the numeric rows so procurement can estimate committed racks.
2) Can Stratus share expected per-tenant split across classes? That will let us convert qps to rack counts and draft an SLA table.
3) Suggest a 30-minute working session (we have availability Wed 09:00–11:00 PT) to align warm-pool policy and failure-mode acceptance.

Attachments: inference_service_classes.csv

—
Priyom Das
Head of Solutions — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-06-11T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stratus / Redwood: dispatching fleet requirements + questionnaire

+1 on Priyom’s draft. A couple of technical clarifications and an ops-friendly tweak: 

On Mon, Jun 10, 2028 at 11:07 AM priyom_das@redwood.ai wrote:
> - Warm pools: keep a configurable prefill corresponding to 15-25% of committed capacity for Classes A/B. Prefill window: 20–45 minutes depending on model load; we recommend a 30-minute default for burst-prone tenants.

Clarifications / additions:
- For sequence-length-dependent models, quantify prefill in token-primed sessions rather than pure QPS. We should provide a small script for estimating token-based priming cost; I'll drop that into the planning folder.
- Admission control: add a soft-QPS thermostat that factors historical prefix cache hit-rate. If cache hit-rate drops > 10% from baseline, throttle batch sizes for Class C first to avoid cascade latency.
- Networking: where possible, pin Class A hosts to racks with isolated uplinks to limit east-west jitter. If Stratus cannot do physical pinning, virtual NIC tagging + ingress shaping will be required.

Operational tweak:
- Add a transient surge bucket that borrows up to 12% of Class B capacity for Class A for up to 10 minutes with automatic reconciliation (billing/commit delta tracked). This avoids uncontrolled preemption while keeping guarantees.

Related link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abcDEFplanning (I’ll add the token-priming script there tonight).

Jonas
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

We’ll confirm Wed 09:30 PT for the working session (confirmed). Procurement wants an itemized CSV they can plug into their cost model — the inference_service_classes.csv you attached looks perfect, please include the committed/burst split and expected headroom %.

Subject: Re: Stratus / Redwood: dispatching fleet requirements + questionnaire — ops notes

Looping in a few operational constraints we must capture in the runbook before procurement signs off: 
- Backpressure and queueing: if admission control rejects inbound requests for > 30s, trigger the incident runbook and auto-scale override; log the rejected request rate to the billing stream for reconciliation.
- Cache-eviction policy: prefer LRU with model-family tagging; eviction storms during heavy churn should trigger selective throttling of large-batch Class C jobs.
- Failure modes and fallbacks: document three concrete fallback tiers (quantized variant, regional reroute, degraded embedding-only response). Each fallback must include guaranteed max-response-size to avoid egress spikes.
- Compliance: maintain audit logs for all model fallbacks and routing policy changes for 365 days (Stratus requirement). We’ll add the policy to JIRA INFRA-9345 and link it to the runbook.

I’ll convert Priyom’s table into an SLA appendix and drop it on the Drive link Jonas shared. Priyom — if you can add the committed-rack projection and the p99 objective for Class A (we default to p99 <= 450ms under committed), I’ll finalize the runbook snippets and post to JIRA.

—
